## Purpose

Recover publication evidence for a retained batch fixer after a daemon restart.
The live owning project or global supervisor and local operator can use this
control. It revalidates authority; it cannot override a hold or withdrawn source.

## Usage

Preview with `aq integration rebind-batch-authority BATCH`. Apply with
`aq integration rebind-batch-authority BATCH --apply --reason "daemon restarted"`.
The response names the bound session and the observed candidate SHA in `evidence`.
The fixer then uses its ordinary `aq integration batch-fix --action push` command.

## Evidence and persistence

The daemon fetches the current Git observation before taking publication locks.
Under the batch row and candidate-ref lease it rechecks current intent, session
identity, frozen members and operator holds. Apply stores `authority_refresh` in
`integration_batches.fixer_state` and emits `integration.batch_authority_rebound`.
Preview leaves that state unchanged. Neither operation changes the checkout,
candidate, frozen members or repair budget. Each push fetches and checks again.

## Refusals

`refused` names missing or withdrawn fixer authority, a stopped/replaced session,
a paused/terminal batch, held or withdrawn sources, unavailable Git evidence, or
a busy/missing candidate ref. Preserve the retained work and resolve the named
condition before retrying. The control never grants target-branch publication or
turns an obsolete source into an eligible one.
